sections.body: Artificial intelligence in research and teaching covers the tools and methods that now sit inside the daily work of scholarship, from searching the literature to running a lab. In practice, AI is used to screen large sets of papers, suggest citations, draft and critique text, code qualitative interviews, model data, and automate repetitive bench tasks. It is also used in classrooms to build exercises and give students faster feedback. The work is less about replacing researchers and more about compressing the slow parts of a project, while leaving judgment, interpretation, and responsibility with people.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some areas are further along than others. Literature search, citation discovery, and quantitative analysis have mature tools and clear workflows, though results still need checking. Qualitative coding, grant writing, and peer review are more contested, because the tasks depend on context and judgment that models handle unevenly. Laboratory automation is real but uneven, and simulation often substitutes for experiment only under narrow conditions. The honest limits are consistent: models can fabricate references, miss nuance, reproduce bias in training data, and obscure how a result was produced. Integrity rules, disclosure, and reproducibility are not solved problems, and no tool removes the need for a human to verify the work.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages move from finding and reading work to producing and governing it. Literature Review and Evidence Synthesis and Citation Mapping and Discovery cover how AI helps locate and organize prior work, while Quantitative Analysis and Reproducible Work and Qualitative Analysis and Mixed Methods deal with analyzing the evidence once it is gathered. Grant Proposals and Funding, Academic Writing and Peer Review, and Course Design and Teaching address the writing, review, and teaching side of academic life. Research Data and Repositories and Laboratory Automation and Simulation cover the data and bench end, where storage, sharing, and automated experiments meet. Governance, Ethics and Research Integrity sits across all of them, because the rules for disclosure, authorship, and verification apply wherever these tools are used. A reader would go to the first pages for discovery, the middle pages for analysis and communication, and the final pages for the standards that hold the rest together.
